"You realize that you just described a completely decentralized, completely anonymous, completely un-censor-able version of ripple [built on bitcoin]?" - Andreas Antonopoulos

There's one major difference though.

In his example, in order to trade, you would have to operate a bot or deploy one on a VPS or on Ethereum or something. First of all, that costs money/resources. And second of all, the bot would be responsible for finding deals, negotiating them and making them.

In Ripple, all you do is issue offers and the Ripple network will automatically take all outstanding offers into account when any transaction is made so that it finds the most beneficial route to make the transaction.
..... The ripple network is full of nodes that do this. S/node/bot and you have the same thing. Bot network = node network.

Right, this market is being made above the protocol level - it's a third layer on top of bitcoin so you've got

bitcoin network = transport layer and digital cash layer

counterparty protocol = tokenized goods / services layer

swapbot protocol = distributed automated fulfillment

You can look at all the active swaps in the system and look for price synergies by hand already here http://tokenrank.tokenly.com/

Here's the open source API that powers it http://apidocs.swapbot.tokenly.com/
